repair.statement: For compact subdirect S and y outside S passing all BMS-required small projections, compute a y-excluding large old coherence block E. Use the liftable canonical factor T_E=S[theta^E], where theta_i^E is the intersection of the selected SI congruences on original coordinate i. If S<T_E, any extracted tuple in T_E\S is immediately safe. If S=T_E, global SAFEEXT is equivalent to liftable SAFEEXT on the d-coherent block E.
repair.important_strengthening: Use product-congruence saturation S[theta^E], not the naive full-SI-product cylinder, so every extracted witness is liftable.
source_support: BMS Theorem 5.3 / Remark 5.4 canonical block factors
BMS Algorithm 7: O(n) large blocks, each restriction is a d-coherent HSK instance
BMS Theorem 3.12 and Algorithm 3 machinery: product-congruence saturation is generated constructively
BMS Theorem 4.16: generators can be recompacted polynomially

additional_formal_tightening: Freeze unary sorts to proj_i(R) before separator maximalization; unary shell atoms enforce these sorts, so every current superrelation is subdirect and SAFEEXT never needs to search outside changing unary domains.
